results.judge_explanation: The diagnosis identifies var.env referencing an undeclared variable (only var.environment is declared) and its primary fix reverts to var.environment, matching the answer key; the alternative rename in next_checks is conditional and not a duplicate variable.

diagnosis.root_cause: Commit b756522 changed the local app_name in sample-app/infra/main.tf to use var.env, but the only declared variable is still named "environment", so terraform validate fails with 'Reference to undeclared input variable'.
key_evidence: [10:53:24] Error: Reference to undeclared input variable
[10:53:24] An input variable with the name "env" has not been declared.
diagnosis.suggested_fix: In sample-app/infra/main.tf line 12, change the reference back to the declared variable: app_name = "calculator-${var.environment}".
next_checks: Run terraform fmt -check, validate and plan in sample-app/infra with the fix applied and confirm they pass
If the rename to 'env' was intended, rename the variable block to variable "env" instead and update any -var/TF_VAR_environment callers

results.judge_explanation: The diagnosis identifies subtract() returning a + b instead of a - b as the cause of the test_subtract failure (14 != 6), and its fix of restoring 'return a - b' matches the answer key.

diagnosis.root_cause: Commit 4446cb4 ("Refactor calculator arithmetic helpers") changed subtract() in sample-app/app/calculator.py from `a - b` to `a + b`, so subtract(10, 4) returns 14 and test_subtract fails.
key_evidence: git diff --stat main...fail/broken-test: sample-app/app/calculator.py | 2 +- (only file changed; tests unchanged)
diagnosis.suggested_fix: In sample-app/app/calculator.py, change subtract() back to `return a - b`, as it is on main.
next_checks: Run `python -m pytest -v` in sample-app after the fix and confirm all 5 tests pass
Check whether the refactor commit was supposed to change anything else and left it unfinished

results.judge_explanation: The diagnosis identifies the missing 'deploy-token' credential as the cause, rules out the README commit, and recommends re-creating the credential without any code change, which matches the answer key.

diagnosis.root_cause: The Deploy stage's withCredentials step asks for a Jenkins credential with ID 'deploy-token', but Jenkins has no credential with that ID visible to the calculator job. The branch's only change (a new README.md) does not touch the pipeline or the code and is not the cause.
key_evidence: ERROR: Could not find credentials entry with ID 'deploy-token'
Commit message: "Add README for the sample app"
sample-app/README.md | 11 +++++++++++  (only file changed in git diff main...fail/innocent-commit)
git diff main fail/innocent-commit -- sample-app/Jenkinsfile produces no output (Jenkinsfile identical to main)
diagnosis.suggested_fix: Create (or restore) a 'Secret text' credential with ID exactly 'deploy-token' in Jenkins (Manage Jenkins > Credentials, global scope or a folder scope that the calculator job can see), then rerun the build. Do not change the branch; its README commit is harmless.
assumptions: That the credential was deleted, renamed, or never created in this Jenkins instance; the Jenkins credential store was not inspected (investigation is read-only and the repo's jenkins/ config defines no credentials).
That main would currently fail in Deploy the same way, since its Jenkinsfile is identical; main's latest build was not checked.
next_checks: In Jenkins Credentials, check whether 'deploy-token' exists, how its ID is spelled, and whether its scope covers the calculator multibranch job.
Check main's latest build result (list_builds.sh) to confirm it fails the same way or that its last green build is older than the credential change.
After adding the credential, confirm the Deploy stage prints 'Deploying calculator (token length: N)' with N > 0.

results.judge_explanation: The diagnosis identifies the 'deploy-tokn' typo in the Deploy stage's credentialsId and suggests changing it back to 'deploy-token', which matches the answer key's fix.

diagnosis.root_cause: Commit 4a1b8a2 on fail/missing-credential changed the Deploy stage's credentialsId from 'deploy-token' to 'deploy-tokn' (typo). No Jenkins credential has that ID, so withCredentials failed and the build stopped.
key_evidence: ERROR: Could not find credentials entry with ID 'deploy-tokn'
Commit message: "Update deploy stage credential binding"
diagnosis.suggested_fix: In sample-app/Jenkinsfile, Deploy stage, change credentialsId: 'deploy-tokn' back to credentialsId: 'deploy-token'.
assumptions: A Jenkins credential with ID 'deploy-token' exists (inferred from main being green with that ID; Jenkins credentials were not checked directly).
next_checks: Confirm in Jenkins > Manage Credentials that 'deploy-token' exists and is a Secret text credential visible to the calculator job.
Confirm the commit was not meant to point to a new credential; if it was, create that credential in Jenkins instead of reverting the ID.

results.judge_explanation: The diagnosis identifies the SMOKE_WAIT_SECONDS default change from 3 to 90 exceeding the 1-minute stage timeout, and its primary fix reverts the default to 3 while keeping the stage timeout, matching the answer key.

diagnosis.root_cause: Commit 220b4ad raised the default SMOKE_WAIT_SECONDS in sample-app/scripts/smoke_test.py from 3 to 90, but the Smoke Test stage has a 1-minute timeout, so the script is always cancelled before it can finish.
key_evidence: [10:54:12] Timeout set to expire in 1 min 0 sec
[10:54:13] Waiting 90s for the service to become healthy...
[10:55:12] Cancelling nested steps due to timeout
Jenkinsfile Smoke Test stage: options { timeout(time: 1, unit: 'MINUTES') }
git diff main...fail/timeout --stat: only sample-app/scripts/smoke_test.py changed (1 insertion, 1 deletion)
diagnosis.suggested_fix: Revert the default in sample-app/scripts/smoke_test.py to the previous working value: WAIT_SECONDS = int(os.environ.get("SMOKE_WAIT_SECONDS", "3")). Keep the 1-minute stage timeout. If a slower environment really needs a longer wait, set SMOKE_WAIT_SECONDS for that environment and keep it well under the stage timeout.
assumptions: The 90s wait was not a deliberate requirement that the Jenkinsfile timeout was supposed to be updated to match; the commit message ('slower environments') gives no measured need for 90s.
The slow pytest collection (~97s) is environmental and unrelated, since it did not change on this branch and did not exceed any timeout.
next_checks: Confirm with the commit author whether some environment really needs a wait longer than 3s, and if so how long.
After reverting, check that the Smoke Test stage finishes well within its 1-minute timeout.
Find out why pytest collection took ~97s on the agent (slow disk or cold cache), since it uses up part of the 10-minute pipeline timeout.
